% Paper 1: the two-constraint frontier R(delta,f) over the (f,delta) plane,
% transcribed from frontier_figure() in
% figures/src/paper1_rdf_frontier_figures.py. The heatmap is a real 21x21
% grid of true_rate(p,f,delta) recomputed directly from the pinned closed
% form (same rate_general as b1_frontier.py); infeasible cells (f<p-delta)
% are set to 0 in the grid and covered by the solid gray triangle drawn on
% top -- exactly the region the script computes as infeasible, since that
% region is bounded by the exact line delta=p-f (f in [0.04,0.05]).
% SIMPLIFICATION FROM THE PNG (noted, not hidden): the original renders the
% infeasible wedge with a matplotlib hatch pattern and draws five thin
% unlabeled contour lines (levels 0.05/0.10/0.15/0.20/0.25) on top of the
% filled heatmap; the hatch and the extra contour isolines are dropped here
% (plain gray fill instead of hatch; no isolines) since reproducing them
% needs either the TikZ `patterns` library (not loaded in the shared
% preamble) or external contour-line computation (pgfplots' contour-from-
% formula path needs gnuplot, unavailable in the CI texlive image) -- purely
% a decorative simplification, not a data change; the colorbar already
% carries the same information the isolines would add.
% COLOUR SCALE CHANGED (noted): the heatmap now carries a fourth data column,
% sqrt(R), used as `point meta`, and the colourbar ticks sit at sqrt
% positions with labels in the original bits/symbol. The z values are
% untouched -- this changes only how R is mapped to lightness, so that the
% two-orders-of-magnitude spread the prose quotes (0.286 against 0.009) is
% readable instead of collapsing into white.
% [verified: script paper1_rdf_frontier_figures.py]
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}
\begin{axis}[
  width=0.78\textwidth,height=6.8cm,
  view={0}{90},
  colormap={whiteharbor}{color=(white) color=(harborblue)},
  % Colour is the weakest visual channel there is, and the prose's headline
  % claim about this surface is a RATIO ("two orders of magnitude between
  % 0.286 and 0.009"), which a linear 0-0.30 ramp cannot show: 0.009 and 0
  % are the same white. The ramp is therefore square-root-transformed --
  % point meta reads a precomputed sqrt(R) column -- and the colourbar ticks
  % are placed at sqrt positions but labelled in the original bits/symbol,
  % so the reader still reads true values off a scale that separates the
  % small ones. Data unchanged; only the colour mapping is nonlinear.
  point meta min=0,point meta max=0.547723,
  colorbar,
  colorbar style={
    ylabel={$R(\delta,f)$ bits/sym ($\sqrt{\cdot}$ colour scale)},
    font=\scriptsize,
    ytick={0,0.1,0.17321,0.24495,0.31623,0.44721,0.54772},
    yticklabels={$0$,$0.01$,$0.03$,$0.06$,$0.10$,$0.20$,$0.30$},
  },
  xlabel={flag rate $f$ (open budget)},
  ylabel={miss budget $\delta$},
  label style={font=\small},
  tick label style={font=\scriptsize},
  title style={font=\small,align=center},
  title={\textbf{The digest--zoom frontier} $R(\delta,f)$: loosening either budget cheapens the digest,\\and past the dashed line it is free [verified closed form]},
  xmin=0.04,xmax=0.16,ymin=0,ymax=0.049,
  axis on top,
]

\caption{The two-constraint frontier $R(\delta,f)$ over the whole $(f,\delta)$ plane near the guarantee corner, from the Proposition's closed form (same formula as \texttt{b1\_frontier.py}). The four numbers of the ``Numbers'' paragraph are marked directly on the surface, including the zero-miss corner that ties this section back to Theorem 1. The dashed line is the Proposition's own boundary $f=1-\delta/p$: below it both constraints bind and the pinned joint applies; above it an $X$-independent flagger already meets the miss budget and $R=0$ exactly, not rising --- the region the corrected geometric-honesty note above refers to. The small grey wedge is simply infeasible ($f<p-\delta$: not enough flag budget to cover the source rate at all).}
\label{fig:rdffrontier}
\end{figure}
